fixes.explanation: That's the oath. The LORD says, “…I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth.” Noah is the man who entered the ark before the floodwaters came (Genesis 7:7). Then He says, “…I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.”

Yes. The LORD says, “This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication is from Me…” declares the LORD. That comes right after He says no weapon formed against her will prosper. He wraps it all up by naming who it's for. It's for His servants.

I understand the doubt, because it sounds backwards. But the text says it's the desolate woman who has more children. The LORD says “…more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband…” Read it again and the bigger number belongs to her.

Yes, friend, and bigger is the whole assignment. The LORD says, “Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings, do not hold back.” Then He adds, “Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes in deep.” That's a woman being told to stop being modest about her floor plan.

A king of Persia is a very fancy guess. But the text never puts a king anywhere in this verse. The LORD says, “For your husband is your Maker—the LORD of Hosts is His name…” That's a husband no throne can top.

Cherished is a lovely word, but it isn't the one in the verse. The LORD says she's like “…a wife deserted and wounded in spirit…” A wounded spirit doesn't sound cherished. That's exactly the one He says He has called back.

Celebrated isn't the word here. The LORD says she's like “…a wife deserted and wounded in spirit, like the rejected wife of one’s youth…” That's how He describes her. And right before it, He says He has called her back.

Mountains do show up in this passage, but not in the LORD's oath. The oath He swore is that “…the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth.” Mountains come in the next verse, where they may be removed but His loving devotion will not depart. Noah is the man who entered the ark before the floodwaters came (Genesis 7:7).

True, and He puts it in the strongest picture around. He says, “Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken…” The mountains may be removed, but His covenant of peace will not be broken.

Cedar and gold sound fancy, but the LORD picks something else. He says, “…I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires.” Then come rubies, sparkling jewels and precious stones. Those are the materials He names.

I see why "only a few" could sound right when you picture a small, hurting city. But the text says all of them. The LORD says, “Then all your sons will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their prosperity.” No son is left out of that.

Yes, they fall. The LORD says, “If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me; whoever assails you will fall before you.” He says an attack on her is not from Him. And whoever assails her is the one who falls before her.
Taking her gates isn't what the LORD says. He says, “whoever assails you will fall before you.” The one who attacks is the one who falls. Nobody walks off with the gates in this verse.
Melting is a pretty picture, but it isn't what the text says. The LORD says, “No weapon formed against you shall prosper…” The weapon is formed against her, and He says it will not prosper.

A good name is worth a lot, but the LORD doesn't say it's the source. He says, “…their vindication is from Me…” declares the LORD. The words are “from Me,” so the source is the LORD Himself. It isn't something the servants carry around on their own.
